newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Leader of Manila leftist death squad arrested.
newsitem.headline: Leader of Manila leftist death squad arrested.

text.p: Philippine police have captured the head of a communist assassination squad linked to the killing of several businessmen and a Singaporean boy in Manila, officials said on Friday.

Joel Castillo, head of the local Communist Party's Alex Boncayao Brigade (ABB), was arrested last weekend, but his capture was not immediately announced so as not to disrupt police operations against the group, national police chief General Recaredo Sarmiento said.
Police said Castillo was carrying a pistol when he was arrested at Manila's harbour, but he did not resist arrest. They gave no other details of his capture.

Castillo was being held under maximum security in a Manila police camp. Charges of illegal possession of firearms were being prepared against him and evidence was being gathered prior to the filing of "more criminal charges," a police statement said.
The statement linked Castillo to the murder of three businessemen, a doctor and two police officers in the Manila area since 1993, and the accidental death of a five-year-old Singaporean boy in 1995.

The boy, visiting Manila with his parents as guests of a local Chinese businessman, was killed when guerrillas fired on the businessman's car, thinking he was inside. But the businessmen was elsewhere and the bullets struck the boy instead.

The police statement said the arrest of Castillo, who had a 500,000-peso ($17,000) bounty on his head, "would create a significant impact" on the ABB, which officials have linked to the killing of hundreds of policemen and local officials in Manila in the past decade.
